paper.abstract_en: This paper continues the exploration of a tachyonic, bosonic string theory in which fermions are not strings, but rather occupy a curved D-brane boundary of open strings, and the open-string tachyon supplies the Higgs sector. The fermionic D-brane occupies the 11 + 1 dimensions of the Clifford algebra $\text {Cl}(11,1)$, while open strings fill out the additional 14 dimensions of a maximal torus of the rank 14 subgroup $\text {SU}(8)_R \times \text {SU}(8)_L$ of the group $G^2(10) = \text {U}(16)$ generated by multivectors of grade 2 (mod 4) in $\text {Cl}(10)$, for a total of $12{+}14 = 26$ dimensions. An important result is that there exist open-string solutions whose D-brane boundary is curved, but those solutions are purely holomorphic (right-moving) or purely antiholomorphic (left-moving) without an associated closed string solution. The only closed-string modes are completely neutral under all internal gauge transformations; for massless modes, these comprise just 4 modes, the spin $\pm 2$ graviton, and two spin 0 modes, the scalar dilaton and the pseudoscalar 2-form.
